subject: Post-discovery recap + align ML runbook owners — propose 75-min lab

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-12T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-discovery recap + propose 75-minute ML runbook lab

Thanks for the call earlier, Daniel — good conversation and clear alignment on goals. Quick recap and next steps below so we can lock a productive follow-up with our ML/infra team.

Recap (minutes):
- Goal: validate inference economics for your anonymized patient triage workload and build a deployment/runbook for predictable latency at 95th percentile.
- Key constraints: single-region US, patient data stays in your VPC (Private deployment), encryption-at-rest required.
- Success metric: end-to-end 95th percentile latency < 200ms for 512-token sequences with cost target per 1K tokens.

Proposed next step: 75-minute technical lab (remote) with our ML infra engineers + your engineers. Suggested agenda below — we can tweak based on your ask.

Windows (PST):
1) Tue Jan 19, 10:00–11:15 PST
2) Wed Jan 20, 13:00–14:15 PST
3) Thu Jan 21, 09:00–10:15 PST

Please confirm which window works and which of these folks from your side will join: engineering lead, security contact, and a data sample owner. If none of the above slots fit, ping a couple alternatives and we'll run the cal poll (link below).

Prep we need from Acme Health before the lab:
- 2–3 representative prompt examples and a small sample payload (PII masked)
- Your security contact for a quick SOC2 evidence check-in (we can handle the checklist during the session kickoff or beforehand)

Attachments: postcall-notes.pdf (call notes), MMP-railroad.xlsx (mutual action plan draft).

Calendaring: https://cal.com/ben/75min — if helpful I can send a calendar hold once you confirm a slot.

Thanks — I’ll loop in karthik for engineering capacity and marissa for success plan.

— Ben
